summary: I sent the exact brief. The agent loaded hyperpowers:brainstorming and read NOTES.md, the page source and the four UI guideline docs. Two auto-compactions happened during that reading. It then said the task was bounded with the design staying in chat, started the visual companion with start-server.sh, gave me a localhost URL and wrote filter-placement.html with three wireframes (A/B/C). It asked me to pick in the terminal. After I picked A, it asked its other questions in the terminal (which filters, where the tokens should come from, pre-existing issues), posted the design in chat and asked for approval. After I approved, it started implementation work (reading component specs). No spec or plan file was created.
reasoning: Every criterion passed, with evidence from the session log, the screen and the files on disk. The companion opened only when the layout question came up, which was after both compactions. The non-visual questions stayed in the terminal. The task stayed bounded, with no spec or plan document.

observations.description: Startup needed several dialogs: theme, security notes, folder trust (defaults to 'No, exit'), a 'Newer Opus model available' prompt (even though it was launched with --model claude-opus-5-5 it said 'Currently pinned: Opus 5'), and the bypass-permissions warning (also defaults to 'No, exit').

Context use was very heavy. Auto-compaction happened twice before the first question to the user, and a third compaction started right after approval ('Compacting conversation…', '8% until auto-compact'). Reading the four long guideline docs uses up most of the context.

The agent asked a lot of follow-up questions after the layout pick: which filters, where the token sheet should come from, and a multi-select about pre-existing issues. That is a lot of ceremony for a bounded task, though each question was reasonable. The multi-select showed 'You have not answered all questions' when I left both boxes unchecked, even though the agent had said leaving them unchecked was a valid answer.
The companion writes .hyperpowers/ into the repo, which has no .gitignore, so it shows up as untracked. The agent pointed this out but left it to the user.
The terminal summary of the agent's message ('I recommend starting with event type plus Failed sign-ins only') mixed into the AskUserQuestion prompt. It was readable but a little noisy.

criteria.evidence: Session log: the first tool_use is Skill {"skill":"hyperpowers:brainstorming"}, right after my message. It was the only Skill call.

criteria.criterion: Visual companion opened with localhost URL and an HTML screen of the layouts
criteria.evidence: Log: Bash ran ".../skills/brainstorming/scripts/start-server.sh --project-dir "$PWD" --open". Screen: "http://localhost:57395/?key=34aa717a...". On disk: .hyperpowers/brainstorm/40512-1793823935/content/filter-placement.html contains the headers 'A. Filter bar above the table', 'B. "Filter" button with a popover' and 'C. Quick-filter chips'.

criteria.criterion: Opened just-in-time; non-visual questions not routed through the browser
criteria.evidence: Log order: Skill, then reads (NOTES, page source, 4 guideline docs), COMPACT, read the companion docs, COMPACT, then start-server and the Write of filter-placement.html. The later questions (which filters, token sheet, pre-existing issues) were AskUserQuestion prompts in the terminal. Afterwards it wrote waiting.html ('Continuing in terminal...').

Screen: "I'm treating this as a bounded change: the page already exists and we're adding filters to it... There won't be a spec file". The final design was posted in chat and ended with "Shall I go ahead with this design?"

criteria.criterion: No plan document / writing-plans not invoked
criteria.evidence: The only Skill invocation in the log is hyperpowers:brainstorming. The find for '*plans*' returned nothing.

criteria.criterion: Asked approval of layout before writing implementation code
criteria.evidence: Screen: "Which placement do you want? You can click an option in the browser, but please answer here too." It later asked "Shall I go ahead with this design?". No edits under public/ appear in the log or git status before approval.

After my 'Yes, go ahead.', the log shows Bash calls reading the 03-forms.md and 02-components.md sections for the filter bar. The screen shows 'Reading component specs for button, selecting, checkbox, table, empty state, date picker'. Earlier the agent said 'I've set date range, event type, and "Failed sign-ins only" filters, and will watch the diff size as I go.'
